$comment: MCP server scorecards, graded per scorecards/RUBRIC.md. Each entry describes the pinned commit only. Do not edit by hand without a grading pass.

sigistry-catalog.name: Sigistry Plugin Catalog

axes.title: Transport
axes.evidence: Single Streamable HTTP endpoint (src/index.js: StreamableHTTPServerTransport, sessionIdGenerator undefined); no HTTP+SSE surface.

axes.title: Stateless core
axes.evidence: A fresh McpServer per request; no session map and no per-IP state. Module-level caches hold only shared public data (marketplace.json, verified.json) with last-good fallback.

axes.title: Lifecycle and protocol version
axes.evidence: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.x handles initialize/negotiation; the only declared capability (tools) is fully implemented (4 tools, all handlers live).

axes.title: Authorization
axes.evidence: Authless by design over read-only public catalog data, which the rubric permits with proportionate abuse controls; every tool now serves cached or static data, so there is no expensive surface to abuse. No downstream token handling of any kind.

axes.title: Tool design
axes.evidence: Complete zod input/output schemas with per-field descriptions; honest annotations (all four tools readOnlyHint, none open-world: verify_plugin returns static instructions); structured isError results; search output capped at 15 rows.

axes.title: Security hygiene
axes.evidence: No subprocess execution anywhere, no filesystem writes, no repository cloning, no user file ingestion; zod validation on all tool arguments; no secrets in the repository; permissive CORS is appropriate for an authless read-only server.

notes: Verification is local-by-design: verify_plugin returns the recipe to run the open-source verifier on the user machine. The server never receives plugin files and never clones repositories (operator policy).
No structured abuse logging or alerting yet; failures are visible only in pm2 logs.

History: v1.3.0 briefly shipped server-side clone-based verification behind rate caps; it was replaced the same day by the local-only design, deleting that entire attack surface rather than defending it.
